newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australia, Indonesia favor China's WTO entry.
newsitem.headline: Australia, Indonesia favor China's WTO entry.

text.p: Indonesia and Australia agreed in principle on Thursday that China should be a member of the World Trade Organisation, Australian Trade Minister Tim Fischer said.
Speaking after a meeting with his Indonesian counterpart Tunky Ariwibowo, Fischer told reporters both countries supported China's admission to the global trade body.
"Indonesia declared that it was, in principle, in full support of China's accession to the WTO," Fischer said after launching a new Australian-built local trunk radio network.

"I declared that Australia was, in principle, in full support of the accession, subject to the completion of the round of investigations in Geneva," said Fischer, who is also Australia's deputy prime minister.

A working group is meeting in Geneva to discuss China's application to join the world trade body. The United States and other Western nations have said that China needs to lower trade barriers before it can join WTO.
Fischer pointed out that after Britain hands back its colony of Hong Kong to China at the end of June 1997, the Customs Union of Hong Kong will be a member of the WTO but not China itself.
"It is very important that China, with its hugely growing economy, become a member of the WTO sooner rather than later," he said.
Fischer, along with five other Australian ministers, is visiting Jakarta for the third Australia-Indonesia Ministerial Forum due to start later on Thursday.
